subject: Fincobank - audit logs & evidence request
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fincobank.com>, Olivia Chu <olivia.chu@fincobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fincobank - audit logs & evidence request

Hi Samir / Olivia -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the follow-ups we committed to: 

1) What you told us: 
- Primary need: demonstrable audit logs for all customer data access (who/what/when) tied to user IDs and service accounts.
- Compliance drivers: internal audit + upcoming regulator review; retention window request: 24 months for customer-facing event logs, 7 years for admin/security events (we noted that may be negotiable).
- PII handling: minimize PII in logs where possible; where present, logs must indicate what fields were accessed and by whom.

2) What Redwood can provide / next steps: 
- We can export audit logs that include timestamps, actor (IAM user/service account), action, resource path, and request/response identifiers. Exports can be CSV/JSONL.
- We have built-in masking options for certain fields and can provide a PIIs-in-logs report showing which fields are present.
- Retention: configurable per-log-type; default retention is 12 months for runtime request logs but we can discuss extended retention on Dedicated/Private deployments or via an export/archival process.

Action items: 
- Samir/Olivia: can you confirm the exact retention windows you need for (a) user access logs and (b) admin/security logs? Also confirm whether you require delivery of historical exports (back to Jan 1, 2024) or just going-forward.
- Alex/Ben: we'll send an export spec and sample CSV/JSONL containing only synthetic data for review (attached).
- Marissa: looping you in from security to answer any technical questions re: masking, entitlement mapping, and export formats.

Attaching: audit_logs_export_spec_v1.csv (sample fields + export options). Also linking our SOC2 summary in case the regulator wants the scope quickly.

If it helps, we can book a 30-min security+infra call this week to walk through the export and masking options - propose Wed/Thu morning PST.

Thanks,

Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachment: audit_logs_export_spec_v1.csv (CSV stub: columns: timestamp,event_id,actor_id,actor_type,action,resource,resource_id,request_id,response_code,field_names_masked)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fincobank.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chu <olivia.chu@fincobank.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Fincobank - audit logs & evidence request

Alex, Ben -

Thanks for the summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifying questions before we loop in our audit team: 

1) Export formats: you mentioned CSV/JSONL - do CSV exports include nested fields (e.g., list of field names accessed) or would that be a separate JSONL payload? Our audit tooling expects a normalized CSV, so if you can provide a CSV with a delimited field for 'fields_accessed' that would be ideal.

2) Retention: we need 24 months for customer-facing access logs (events where customer data may have been viewed/exported) and 7 years for admin/security logs. If Redwood's default is 12 months, what's the path to retain 24/84 months? Is this handled via an export+archive or do you provide native retention configuration at the account level?

3) PII: when you say masking, can you outline whether masking is redaction at logging time (no raw field saved) vs storage-level tokenization/encryption? Our auditors will want to understand whether the raw values ever exist in any persistent storage.

4) Historical exports: we need logs back to Jan 1, 2024 for a scoped set of resources (user data access events for two product lines). Can you confirm whether you can produce a historical export for that window and an estimated file size / transfer method?

Finally - timeline: our audit team wants the exports and a write-up by Jul 14 if possible. Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Samir
Director of IT Audit, Fincobank
samir.patel@fincobank.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fincobank.com>, Olivia Chu <olivia.chu@fincobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 12:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fincobank - audit logs & evidence request

Samir -

Answers inline below and next steps. Short version: we can meet your Jul 14 target for a scoped deliverable if we get confirmation on scope this week.

1) Export formats: CSV will include a delimited field (pipe-separated) for 'fields_accessed' to handle lists. We also provide JSONL exports for richer nested metadata. We'll include a sample CSV row in the attached spec showing how the delimited field looks.

2) Retention: native retention is configurable per-account in Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted accounts, default is 12 months; extended retention (24/84 months) can be achieved via scheduled exports to a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket or via our Dedicated retention policy for enterprise contracts. If you want native 7-year retention on hosted, we'll need a contract amendment (we can propose an archival plan).

3) PII handling: two modes - (a) redaction at ingest (no raw value is stored for configured fields), or (b) encrypted storage with strict key-management. By default hosted logs retain raw values for troubleshooting for a short window (30 days) and then persist masked versions. However, for regulated customers we recommend either redaction-at-ingest or sending exports to your encrypted archive (S3 with SSE-KMS). Marissa (security) - can chime in with technical specifics.

4) Historical exports: we can generate an export for Jan 1, 2024 -> present for scoped resources. Estimated size: rough ballpark 45-120 GB depending on the scope and sampling. Transfer options: secure S3 upload, encrypted GCS bucket, or temporary SharePoint SFTP drop. Let us know your preferred target.

Next steps (proposed):
- Samir: confirm scope (list of resource IDs / product lines) and preferred transfer target by EOD Wed (Jul 8).
- Marissa/Ben: we'll prepare a short technical write-up (1-2 pages) describing masking modes, key management, and evidence artifacts (sample exported CSV, access-control mapping, retention policy screenshots).
- Schedule: on receipt of scope, we'll queue the historical export and aim to deliver a scoped sample and write-up by Jul 14.

Attaching: updated audit_logs_export_spec_v1.csv (includes CSV sample row and field definitions).

Thanks -
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fincobank.com>, Olivia Chu <olivia.chu@fincobank.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fincobank - audit logs & evidence request

Hi Samir / Olivia -

Quick follow-up from security/controls side:

- Redaction vs encryption: for redaction-at-ingest we never persist the raw value for configured field patterns (SSNs, full PANs, raw government IDs). Those fields are replaced with a deterministic hash and an indicator column (e.g., field_masked=true). For encryption we use customer-managed KMS keys where required (we support AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault).

- Evidence artifacts we can provide: export CSV/JSONL (sample), access-control mapping (CSV), IAM audit reports showing who accessed the export and when, and a short screencapture/video showing the export job run.

- Historical export ETA: once Samir provides a scope list, we can provide an exact ETA - typical turnaround for a scoped 50-100 GB export is 3-5 business days. We will stage the export to your target bucket; events will be partitioned by date to make processing easier.

I'll put together the technical write-up and a checklist for your auditors and share by EOD Wed. If helpful, suggest a 30-minute call Thu 10am PST to walk the audit team through the artifacts.

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
